section_summary: This section follows the proposed Grand Yokohama Exposition from the city's 1934 invitation and exhibition regulations through United States departmental responses. A consul's April 1935 report describes the opened exposition as chiefly a Japanese commercial display, with few foreign exhibits and practical difficulties for the adjacent American Consulate.

people.name: Ichiro Ohnishi
people.role: Mayor of Yokohama and president of the exposition

people.name: Tokugoro Tanabe
people.role: Chairman of the Yokohama Municipal Assembly and exposition vice president

people.name: Suyekichi Nakagawa
people.role: Vice president of the Yokohama Chamber of Commerce and Industry and exposition vice president

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs suggestion on American participation
subfiles.about: Recommends considering American participation after formal notification clarifies the exposition's official status.
subfiles.summary: Favors participation as a reciprocal courtesy, but advises awaiting formal Japanese notification.

subfiles.title: Consular despatch on the Yokohama Municipal Exposition
subfiles.about: Transmits correspondence and site materials while explaining the city's interest in American exhibits and visitors.
subfiles.summary: Boyce reports proposed dates, customs treatment and exhibitor costs. He directs the mayor toward Japanese diplomatic channels for requests and notes that the site surrounds two sides of the consulate.

subfiles.title: Mayor's invitation concerning the Yokohama exposition
subfiles.about: Requests that the United States be informed of and lend moral support to the planned reconstruction exposition.
subfiles.summary: The mayor presents the exposition as a commemoration of recovery from the 1923 disaster and a way to encourage trade.

subfiles.title: Consul's reply to Mayor Ohnishi
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the invitation and suggests channels for seeking American exhibits.
subfiles.summary: Boyce promises to inform the Department of State and recommends using Japanese representatives in the United States to solicit exhibits.

subfiles.title: Exposition site plans
subfiles.about: Shows the exposition grounds and nearby streets and buildings.
subfiles.summary: Plans locate exhibition buildings beside the waterfront and American Consulate.

subfiles.title: Yamashita Park exposition site
subfiles.about: Identifies Yamashita Park as a proposed exposition site.
subfiles.summary: Photograph caption identifies Yamashita Park as a proposed site.

subfiles.title: Exposition grounds diagram
subfiles.about: Diagrams exhibition buildings and attractions.
subfiles.summary: Diagram marks exhibition buildings, entrances and attractions.

subfiles.title: Consular despatch transmitting exposition regulations
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of the exposition regulations.
subfiles.summary: Boyce forwards regulations and notes the grounds border three sides of the consulate.

subfiles.title: Regulations of the Grand Yokohama Exposition in Commemoration of Its Reconstruction
subfiles.about: Sets out the exposition's purpose, schedule, exhibit categories, fees and operating rules.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet presents the exposition as a celebration of Yokohama's recovery and a means to promote domestic and foreign trade. It lists exhibit categories and specifies applications, space charges, delivery dates, sales procedures, admission fees and exhibitor responsibilities. Its stated March 26–May 24, 1935 period differs from the dates in the mayor's earlier letter.

subfiles.title: Japanese diplomatic request for United States participation
subfiles.about: Asks the Secretary to help secure United States product exhibits for the exposition.
subfiles.summary: The note requests American participation and describes Yokohama's reconstruction and international industrial cooperation as the exposition's aims.

subfiles.title: State Department referral to Agriculture
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese note and pamphlets and asks for appropriate publicity.
subfiles.summary: Requests publicity for the exposition and its invitation to foreign exhibitors.

subfiles.title: State Department referral to Commerce
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese materials for publicity through the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce.
subfiles.summary: Asks Commerce to publicize the exposition to possible exhibitors.

subfiles.title: State Department referral to Interior
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese materials and asks for appropriate publicity.
subfiles.summary: Asks Interior to publicize the exposition and possible exhibits.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the invitation and reports referral to relevant United States departments.
subfiles.summary: States that the exposition has been brought to departments able to alert possible exhibitors.

subfiles.title: Agriculture Department response
subfiles.from: M. L. Wilson, Acting Secretary of Agriculture
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the exposition invitation and refers it to the department's press service.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture will consider issuing a news release for American producers.

subfiles.title: Interior Department response on publicity
subfiles.from: Oscar L. Chapman, Assistant Secretary of the Interior
subfiles.about: Reports that Interior bureaus have been advised of the exposition.
subfiles.summary: Interior has no participation funds but has informed its bureaus.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department response
subfiles.about: Promises to notify district offices and publish an exposition notice.
subfiles.summary: Commerce will alert district offices and announce the event in Commerce Reports.

subfiles.title: Interior Department response on providing an exhibit
subfiles.about: Declines to furnish material for the exposition because of limited facilities and funds.
subfiles.summary: Interior cannot forward an exhibit or fund its participation.

subfiles.title: Japanese Ambassador's acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of a copy of the Department's response to the October 1934 Japanese note.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador thanks State for the requested copy.

subfiles.title: Copy of State Department reply transmitted to the Japanese Ambassador
subfiles.about: Sends a copy of the Department's October 1934 reply concerning the exposition.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the requested copy after an Embassy telephone conversation.

subfiles.title: Consular report on the opened Grand Yokohama Exposition
subfiles.about: Assesses the opened exposition, foreign participation and its effects on the consulate.
subfiles.summary: Boyce finds the exposition chiefly a Japanese commercial display with only a few foreign exhibits, despite efforts to attract American cities. He describes military displays, crowded streets and sanitation concerns around the consulate. Wet weather has hurt receipts and an American rodeo, whose performers sought consular help over pay.

subfiles.title: Consular transmittal of Japan Times and Mail exposition issue
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of an April 28 newspaper issue describing the exposition.
subfiles.summary: Forwards five copies of The Japan Times and Mail.

subfiles.title: Key to Yokohama exposition vicinity
subfiles.about: Lists landmarks surrounding the exposition site.
subfiles.summary: Numbered key identifies the consulate, public buildings, businesses, park and exposition.
